chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm from Abd Allah ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah from his father, upon them be peace, who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man divorces his wife, he has more right to her as long as she has not performed the ritual bath from the third [divorce].'

key_terms.أَحَقُّ بِهَا: has more right to her / is more entitled to her

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a husband's right to revoke divorce according to Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies the condition for the finality of the third divorce, asserting that the husband's right to revocable retraction (raj'a) persists until the wife completes the ritual bath (ghusl) following the third pronouncement. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the third talaq does not become irrevocably binding until the completion of this specific physical act, distinguishing it from the second talaq where the waiting period alone suffices. It underscores the precision in Shia fiqh regarding the temporal markers that finalize marital dissolution.
